Sample Key Construction: This is the Excel file I have been using to tinker with quotients for cipher keys. I had to build the dividing "Mill" because Excel only gives you 15 decimal places in a number display, and I wanted A2 thru QO 192 protected. Row 1 is open for inputs, below 192 available for experimenting. Past Col QP Values Here A8 thru OZ700 protected, rest is free to fiddle with. A8 thru OZ600 protected, rest open. Special Paste Value of Z3 here: Special Paste Value of Z6 here: Special Paste Value of Z7 here: I have locked up the formulas to keep them from accidental destruction, but you can still use them. Most of the places you might want to go have been named, and the name box will scoot you there This file is not warranted as fit for any purpose whatever, unless your purpose is using up lots of time making numbers do gymnastics for you. Feel free to copy, if it looks useful, and if the locked cells give you trouble, ask me to send you a copy & I'll happily do so - they are locked not because I want to keep them for myself forever, but so that somebody doesn't stomp around in them so that the formulas don't work for the next guy who might want to use it. If I send you an unlocked version, have lists of quotients someplace, but this can still be handy. As you will see, I have hardly scratched I'm sure computer people have more elegant versions of this, and number theory people probably the surface here - mostly confined myself to prime divisors, and 1 for the dividend. The universe :) Carl Ellis quickly. Put your test dividend & divisor in the boxes named TEST_DIVIDEND and TEST_DIVISOR and the computer does the rest. Plenty of room at the bottom of the QUOTIENTS and REMAINDERS tabs for recording interesting finds. to be able to fiddle with the digits individually anyway, look at the remainders at each step and collectively, &c.
